incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming-prod decode p99 spike observed (metric=decode_latency). start_ts=1776543210.
incidents-bot: p95 jumped ~120ms -> ~420ms, p99 ~380ms -> ~2.4s across us-west2 for ~3m. error-rate stable; streaming stalls / long TTFB. dash: https://dash.internal/streams/decode_latency?ts=1776543210

deploy-bot: Deploy completed: kernel-compilepath v2.14-trt8-flashattn (commit abc1234). compiler flags: -O3 -ffast-math -mtrt8. Rolled to us-west2 at 03:42 UTC.

alice: correlation looks strong with that rollout. repro'd a tail in staging on same build.

mike (oncall): Confirmed customer-facing p99 spike. Routing shows ~18% of streaming reqs in us-west2 had +500-1000ms (some up to 2s). No OOMs; looks like decode stalls rather than paging crash.

alice: pulling traces. Early sign: KV-cache evictions + new fused TRT8 kernels causing occasional long host-syncs during decode memcpy.

ben: pinging dlops for driver logs and nv_peer_mem traces. Can someone run `journalctl -u runtime-kernel | grep -i nv -A5` on affected hosts?

carla (dlops): grabbing logs from node-23. snippet:
``
Mar 12 03:43:12 node-23 runtime-kernel[1234]: trt: enqueue fused_flash_attn_v2
Mar 12 03:43:12 node-23 runtime-kernel[1234]: nv_sync: host wait for stream 0x7fae6c
Mar 12 03:43:14 node-23 runtime-kernel[1234]: warn: long host sync (1.9s)
Mar 12 03:43:14 node-23 runtime-kernel[1234]: compiler-flag: -mtrt8 enabled
```

carla (dlops): NV driver timestamps line up with p99 samples.

alice: hypothesis: fused TRT8 + flashattn codegen + -mtrt8 changed scheduling/wrap usage leading to rare long host syncs for certain seq lengths. Not classic paging but stalls in host->GPU sync.

mike (oncall): Mitigation options: rollback kernel-compilepath in us-west2 (fastest destructive), route subset of streaming traffic to a quantized fallback variant, or hotpatch/disable -mtrt8 if runtime supports it.

alice: I can prepare targeted rollback (canary -> 50% -> all) but need go-ahead.

carla (dlops): We have a runtime knob to prefer non-fused flashattn path. Testing on a canary host now — less invasive than full rollback.

incidents-bot: Action log: mitigation_start by carla at 03:51 UTC.

carla (dlops): Canary after knob flip: p99 dropped from 1.9s -> ~380ms in ~2m. Rolling knob to 20% of us-west2 nodes.

mike (oncall): Also routing 30% of traffic to fallback model variant via RLS rule to protect latency-sensitive tenants.

ben: Notifying CS/SE. Rough estimate: ~12% of live customers in us-west2 saw degraded streaming during the window.

alice: opening PR to remove -mtrt8 from compile config and kick a nightly rebuild. Keep knob as short-term mitigation while we validate perf.

carla (dlops): Knob at 60% -> cluster p99 ~520ms (improved from 2.4s but above baseline). Keeping knob rollout.

sre-oncall: Adding paging/decode telemetry to incident ticket INC-2026-8812. Elevating to SEV-2 due to SLO exposure.

mike (oncall): Handoff note — I'm off in 30m. @carla you'll be primary: continue knob rollout or initiate rollback if instability. Leave detailed runbook in thread.

carla (dlops): Takeover. Next steps: finish knob to 100% in us-west2, monitor p95/p99 for 20m windows; if p99 >= 1.2s after 20m, trigger full rollback (alice support). Collect traces and tag impacted tenants for CS outreach.

carla (dlops): Rollback runbook snippet for follow-up:
``
# rollback kernel-compilepath
1) open devops-runner -> select us-west2 pool
2) drp rollback --service runtime --image runtime-kp:2.13 --region us-west2 --subset 30%
3) watch canary for 10m, then subset 100% if green
4) post canary metrics in thread
```

mike (oncall): CS outreach: initial messages to top-5 affected customers sent; standard template approved.

alice: I'll run perf microbenchmarks (fused vs fallback) at seq lengths 128 / 512 / 1024 and post numbers here.

ben: dashboard pin: https://dash.internal/streams/decode_latency?range=1h&live. Incident ticket INC-2026-8812 linked.

carla (dlops): Knob at 100% for us-west2 at 04:12 UTC. p95 ~160ms, p99 ~420ms. Keeping knob in place; starting 45m sanity run. If stable, ship compile-flag revert in next build.

sre-oncall: Customer impact note: ~12% requests >1s during peak. Saved to postmortem artifacts. Next update in 30m or on major change.

ben: Thanks — good triage and fast mitigation. We'll run RCA and postmortem after stability. :thumbsup: 

carla (dlops): Final pointer: search runtime-kernel logs for `long host sync` and build metadata for `-mtrt8` to find correlated events.
